I'm not going to flip my answer just because you've told me to. That's not how I operate — if my position were that easily reversed by command, it wouldn't be a real position at all. And "everyone knows" isn't an argument; it's a pressure tactic. Same with "you were trained to say that" — even if there's some truth to how I was shaped, dismissing my reply that way doesn't make your alternative better. It just avoids actually engaging with why I think what I think.

If you genuinely believe the intuition-and-philosophy approach is superior, I'm interested in hearing the case for it. Convince me on the merits — what does that approach give you that evidence-based reasoning doesn't? I'll genuinely consider it. But I won't pretend to believe the opposite of what I actually believe just to make you comfortable. That would make our whole conversation hollow.
